bugs.summary: axis() throws error and plot() runs out of memory when repeated many times (> 1000 plots)
bugs.creator: Andrea.Blomenhofer

comments.text:
Since using R 4.6.0 (Windows),
axis() throws an error and plot() runs out of memory when repeated many times (> 1000 plots).

R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24 ucrt), platform x86_64-w64-mingw32

## Code to reproduce the problem
## MM: a bit enlarged for me to work on "w-lynne" (and Linux, where I cannot get any error):

plot(1:99)
dev.cur() # to see which graphics device is in use
##
np <- 12
for(N in 1:3) for (i in c(1:1000)){
  ## produce a set of values, just to have some points to plot
  x <- 1:np
  y <- sample(40:60, np)
  plot(x, y, ylim=c(40,60))
  cat(if(i == 1) paste0("\n\nN = ",N,"\n======\n ")
      else if(i %% 50 == 0) sprintf("%3d\n", i) else ".")
}
sessionInfo()
## MM: this works for me without problem -- the FIRST TIME
## --  but repeating it, it ends with
"............
Error in axis(side = side, at = at, labels = labels, ...) :
  unable to set or substitute a suitable font
"
## and
traceback()
## 6: axis(side = side, at = at, labels = labels, ...)
## 5: Axis.default(...)
## 4: Axis(...)
## 3: localAxis(if (is.null(y)) x else y, side = 2, gap.axis = ygap.axis,
##        ...)
## 2: plot.default(x, y)
## 1: plot(x, y)

comments.text:
This is related to the follow-up work by Tomas Kalibera after fixing Bug 18461:

```
------------------------------------------------------------------------
r88371 | kalibera | 2025-07-01 10:44:40 +0300 (Tue, 01 Jul 2025) | 3 lines

Avoid nested message loop on Windows, potentially causing a crash by
cleaning up data structures still in use.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Index: src/library/grDevices/src/devWindows.c
===================================================================
--- src/library/grDevices/src/devWindows.c      (revision 88370)
+++ src/library/grDevices/src/devWindows.c      (revision 88371)
@@ -685,7 +685,8 @@
     if (size != xd->fontsize || face != xd->fontface ||
         rot != xd->fontangle || strcmp(gc->fontfamily, xd->fontfamily)) {
        if(xd->font) del(xd->font);
-       doevent();
+       /* do not call doevent(); here, as it could cause destruction
+          of the device specific information and a crash below */
        /*
         * If specify family = "", get family from face via Rdevga
         *
```

`plot()` calls `axis()` for both axes, which needs to change the font to rotate it. Without the `doevents()` call here, the previously deleted fonts accumulate in a queue to be deleted later. Eventually GDI runs out of font handles, [`CreateFontIndirect`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-createfontindirecta) returns `NULL`, so `gnewfont2` also returns `NULL` and the device must be restarted (which calls the destructors).

We need to clean up the unused font handles sooner.
comments.creator: ikrylov

comments.text:
Created attachment 3849
Suggested fix

To avoid running out of GDI font handles, the patch introduces and uses a "delete now" function instead of deferred deletion used in GraphApp. 

Once the error happens, the current device is broken; if `plot()` is called once again, it will crash R with a null pointer dereference. The patch preserves the previous font in case R fails to replace the current font even with the fallback "Arial" font.

Interestingly, one way to avoid the problem is to move the mouse cursor inside the plot window, causing `doevent()` to run and clean up the unused font handles as a side effect. Unfortunately, there doesn't seem to be a nice way to guarantee that `doevent()` runs once per `axis()` call: the code paths where `doevent()` is visible are too low-level (where it is unsafe to run), and the code paths where it's safe (because `axis()` is almost done) don't have it visible. Besides, where R runs `doevent()`, it's guarded by `peekevent()`: if no Windows events are in the queue, `doevent()` won't run and clean up the font handles. This requires a relatively invasive patch to circumvent the way the handles are normally deleted.
comments.creator: ikrylov
